key_insight: Loop Dropout regularizes shared LoRA updates in looped language models by randomly masking adapter applications with inverse-survival rescaling, reducing late-loop bias and improving adaptation across all loop positions.
engineering_relevance: It is a drop-in training-time regularizer for looped LLMs that keeps inference unchanged while improving mathematical reasoning, instruction tuning, and code generation.
method: Stochastically omit adapter applications across loop iterations during training
Rescale active updates by inverse survival probability to preserve expected update strength
Train shared updates to be effective under varied loop-application patterns
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments across model sizes, adapter ranks, and training recipes, with consistent gains in mathematical reasoning and additional improvements on instruction tuning and code generation.
watch_item: The method adds stochastic training complexity and its benefit depends on preserving the correct rescaling; naive dropout without inverse-survival scaling does not improve performance.
paper_title: Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models
